deep.reconstruction:
Notation: in E477 Euler writes ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) for the inclusive double sum Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m}(1+2^{-n}+…+z^{-n}). In modern terms this is the multiple zeta-star value ζ*(m,n) = ζ(m,n)+ζ(m+n). ∫1/z^k is ζ(k). The page finishes the 'fifth order', weight m+n=6.

Write A=ζ*(2,4), B=ζ*(3,3), C=ζ*(4,2), D=ζ*(5,1), P=ζ(4)ζ(2), Q=ζ(3)², Z=ζ(6). Euler has five linear equations:
- E1 (previous page; case m=5, n=1 after the divergent ζ(1)ζ(5) terms are cancelled against the 'first method'): A+B+C+D = 4P−2Z.
- E2 (case m=4, n=2, finished at the top of this page): A+2B+4C+8D = 9P+Z.
- E3 (case m=n=3): 2B+6C+12D = 12P+Q−Z.
- E4 and E5 (the 'first method', i.e. the reflection or stuffle relation ζ*(a,b)+ζ*(b,a)=ζ(a)ζ(b)+ζ(a+b)): A+C = P+Z and 2B = Q+Z.

He solves for the four unknowns:
- D = 3P − Q/2 − (7/2)Z
- C = −(16/3)P + Q + 9Z
- B = Q/2 + Z/2
- A = (19/3)P − Q − 8Z

The system is overdetermined. Feeding the solution into the leftover equation gives ζ(6) = (4/7)ζ(2)ζ(4). He checks this against ζ(2)=π²/6, ζ(4)=π⁴/90 and ζ(6)=π⁶/945.

The purpose is the paper's programme: evaluate all double Euler sums of a given weight in terms of zeta values. Along the way, the two independent families of relations (the 'second method', a partial-fraction or shuffle-type relation, and the 'first method', the stuffle/reflection relation) force a known relation among even zeta values.
errors: The coefficient of ∫1/z^6 in the formula for ∫(1/z^2)(1/y^4) must be −8. This is fixed by A+C=P+Z and by the known value ζ*(2,4)=37/12 ζ(6)−ζ(3)². In the scan it looks like '3'; either it is a misprint or the scan is illegible there.

Euler says the final relation comes from 'aequationem primo inventam' (E1). But his solution formulas satisfy E1, E2, E4 and E5 identically. It is E3 (case m=n=3) that is not satisfied symbolically: it gives 4P+Q+13Z = 12P+Q−Z, i.e. Z=(4/7)P. The expressions are therefore only determined modulo this relation, and the attribution of the extra equation is loose.
All four evaluations are correct once the relation is used: ζ*(5,1)=7/4ζ(6)−½ζ(3)², ζ*(4,2)=ζ(3)²−⅓ζ(6), ζ*(3,3)=½(ζ(3)²+ζ(6)), ζ*(2,4)=37/12ζ(6)−ζ(3)². The relation ζ(6)=4/7ζ(2)ζ(4) is also true.

ideas.what: Closed forms of all weight-6 depth-2 inclusive Euler sums in terms of ζ(3)², ζ(2)ζ(4) and ζ(6)
ideas.modern_name: evaluation of double zeta(-star) values of weight 6
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1776); revisited by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and Flajolet–Salvy (1998)

ideas.what: Combining the reflection identity with the partial-fraction ('second method') identities of the same weight; the overdetermined system yields a relation among single zeta values
ideas.modern_name: double shuffle relations implying even-zeta relations (cf. Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier 2006)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for the method; modern formalisation by Zagier, Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier, Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier
ideas.where_published: E477 (same paper, also at weight 4 earlier)

ideas.what: Cancellation of the divergent terms ζ(1)ζ(5) between two identities before solving
ideas.modern_name: regularization of divergent multiple zeta values (regularized double shuffle)

missed.claim: Euler explicitly observes that his two families of relations for double sums (essentially shuffle and stuffle), together with cancellation of divergent ζ(1)-terms, are overdetermined and force ζ(6)=4/7 ζ(2)ζ(4). This prefigures the modern result that regularized double shuffle produces the even-zeta (Bernoulli) relations. The idea is fairly well recognised in the MZV literature as originating in E477, so it is likely not genuinely missed.
missed.quote: tum vero aequationem primo inuentam adhibendo obtinetur ∫1/z^6 = 4/7 ∫1/z^4·∫1/z^2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the double-shuffle-implies-even-zeta phenomenon; probably already acknowledged in surveys of Euler sums.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, known Euler evaluations of weight-6 double sums from E477, which are well documented. The derivation of ζ(6)/ζ(2)ζ(4) from an overdetermined system is a nice early double-shuffle phenomenon but is largely recognised.
transcription_corrections: In the last formula for ∫(1/z^2)(1/y^4), the image appears to print '− 3∫1/z^6'; the mathematically correct coefficient is −8, so the transcription's '−8' should be flagged as a correction of the print or scan.
The image shows '+ 19/3' with a leading plus sign, and '1/2∫1/z^3·∫1/z^3' (rendered '½'), matching the transcription.
